alerts.headline: Wind Advisory issued September 27 at 5:20AM HST until September 27 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
* WHAT...East winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Oahu, Kauai, and Niihau. The strongest winds are expected
on Oahu, especially over and downwind of terrain.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Winds this strong can tear off shingles, knock down tree
branches, blow away tents and awnings and make it difficult to
steer, especially for drivers of high profile vehicles.
alerts.instruction:
Watch out for falling tree branches when walking or driving. Make
sure tents and awnings are secure or take them down. Be prepared for
power outages.

alerts.headline: High Wind Warning issued September 27 at 5:20AM HST until September 27 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
* WHAT...East winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 75 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of Maui, Big Island, Molokai, and Lanai over and
downwind of terrain, especially in west Maui and Kohala.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds may blow down trees and power lines and
damage roofs. Power outages are possible. Travel will be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.
alerts.instruction:
Strong winds may lead to property damage. Hazardous driving
conditions due to powerful cross winds will pose a serious risk for
drivers, especially for light weight and high profile vehicles. Loose
outdoor items should be brought inside or secured properly.

A High Wind Warning means that winds are expected to be at least 40
mph, with gusts over 60 mph. Stay away from downed power lines.

alerts.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 27 at 3:49AM HST until September 27 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR EAST FACING SHORES OF MOLOKAI,
MAUI, AND THE BIG ISLAND THROUGH THIS EVENING...

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR SOUTHEAST FACING SHORES OF
THE BIG ISLAND THROUGH THIS EVENING...

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR EAST FACING SHORES OF KAUAI
AND OAHU THROUGH MONDAY MORNING...

.Southeast swell generated by Hurricane Nolo is beginning to decline
for the Big Island, but continues to produce advisory level surf for
east and southeast facing shores. This swell combined with
gale-force trades is producing advisory level surf along east
facing shores of Maui, Molokai, Oahu and Kauai. Surf will
diminish below advisory criteria later today for the eastern
islands but will likely continue through tonight for Oahu and
Kauai as Nolo moves westward away from the islands.

* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft in the morning,
diminishing to 7 to 10 ft by this evening.

* WHERE...East facing shores of Molokai, Maui, and the Big
Island.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
alerts.instruction:
Heed all advice from ocean safety officials. When in doubt, don't
go out.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM HST Sun Sep 27 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located southwest of Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, on recently
downgraded Tropical Storm Odalys, located well west of the southern
tip of Baja California, on Hurricane Nolo, located a few hundred
miles south-southwest of the Big Island of Hawaii, and on Tropical
Depression Eighteen-E, located several hundred miles southwest of
the Acapulco, Mexico.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure associated with persistent showers and
thunderstorms is currently located well east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands. Environmental conditions are expected to be
conducive for further development, and a tropical depression is
likely to form in the next several days. The system should move
generally northeastward, and remain well east-southeast of  the
Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...50 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Eighteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Eighteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP3.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Papin

aiBriefing: Dziś na Hawajach obowiązują ostrzeżenia przed silnym wiatrem i wysokim przybojem, spowodowane głównie przez huragan Nolo przechodzący w pobliżu wysp oraz silne pasaty. Wszystkie te alerty kończą się jeszcze dzisiaj lub jutro rano, czyli na długo przed Waszym przylotem za 4 dni (2 października) — powinny więc całkowicie ustąpić, zanim zaczniecie podróż. Sam huragan Nolo oddala się na zachód od wysp i traci na sile. Jest jeszcze potencjalny nowy system tropikalny rozwijający się daleko na wschód-południowy wschód od Hawajów (80% szans uformowania w 7 dni), ale prognoza mówi, że ma pozostać z dala od wysp, więc na razie nie jest to bezpośrednie zagrożenie dla Waszej trasy po Oahu, Big Island i Maui. Poziom zagrożenia 2 (Podwyższony) odzwierciedla dzisiejszą sytuację, nie to, co zastaniecie po przylocie — warto tylko śledzić rozwój tego nowego systemu bliżej daty wyjazdu.

aiUnnamedSystem.description: Szeroki obszar niskiego ciśnienia z burzami, opisany jako położony daleko na wschód-południowy wschód od Hawajów, z wysoką (80%) szansą uformowania się w cyklon tropikalny w ciągu 7 dni; prognoza wskazuje ruch na północny wschód, czyli dalej od wysp.
